paperTitle: Evaluation of Pose Estimation for Fall Detection Systems
centralContribution: This work evaluates the effectiveness of pose estimation methods as a feature extraction solution for fall detection systems, demonstrating that combining state-of-the-art pose estimation frameworks with a simple neural network classifier achieves competitive results against sensor and other camera-based solutions on the UR Fall Detection dataset.

gameObjects.visualMetaphor: This work evaluates the effectiveness of pose estimation methods as a feature extraction solution for fall detection systems, demonstrating that combining state-of-the-art pose estimation frameworks with a simple neural network classifier achieves competitive results against sensor and other camera-based solutions on the UR Fall Detection dataset.

Falls among the elderly are a leading cause of injury, necessitating effective fall detection. Existing solutions like wearables or ambient sensors have limitations. Traditional camera-based methods are often complex or require specialized hardware. This paper proposes using pose estimation, a hardware-agnostic method, to extract semantic-rich human joint location information from standard RGB video as features for fall detection.

A conceptual illustration of the proposed system pipeline, where raw RGB video frames are processed by one of three state-of-the-art pose estimation frameworks (OpenPose, AlphaPose, PoseNet) to extract 3 * K pose feature vectors. These vectors are then fed into a simple fully-connected neural network classifier, which outputs a fall probability via a sigmoid activation function.

This figure likely illustrates the three data modes—RGB, Depth, and Acceleration—available in the UR Fall Detection dataset, possibly showing example frames or data representations for each mode. The paper's method primarily utilizes the RGB data from this dataset.
